items.title: Lean verification of the Riemann Hypothesis
items.summary: Researchers have successfully employed Lean, a proof assistant, to verify aspects of the Riemann Hypothesis, a long-standing problem in mathematics. This development highlights the increasing role of AI in formal verification and mathematical proofs, which could inspire new approaches in software engineering and algorithm design.

items.title: PostgreSQL Extensions in Go
items.summary: A new project has been released that allows developers to create PostgreSQL extensions using the Go programming language, enhancing the flexibility and performance of database interactions. This could significantly streamline backend development processes for web applications that rely on PostgreSQL.

items.title: Brazil's tax authority open-sources its tax calculator on GitHub under MIT
items.summary: Brazil's tax authority has made its tax calculator available as open-source software on GitHub, promoting transparency and collaboration in public sector software development. This initiative could serve as a model for other governments looking to enhance public service efficiency through open-source solutions.

items.title: Inkling-2-Mini in 5.4 GB Memory
items.summary: The Inkling-2-Mini model has been released with a compact size of just 5.4 GB, making advanced AI capabilities more accessible for developers working on resource-constrained environments. This development is significant for the deployment of AI applications in mobile and edge computing scenarios.

items.title: Show HN: Zero C# – C# without a runtime or GC
items.summary: A new project called Zero C# has been introduced, allowing developers to write C# code without the need for a runtime or garbage collection. This could lead to significant performance improvements and lower resource consumption in applications where efficiency is critical.
